title: Open world — solo, 200 turns
description: A 64-by-64 open world stretches around you. The ground is mostly grass, with a small lake to the south of center, four scattered tree clusters, and a large rocky hill in the northeast that climbs partway into the second layer. Iron-ore deposits sit inside the hill. You have 200 turns. There is no goal, no storm, no required outcome — the world will simply pause when your time is up.
goal: You have 200 turns in this open world. Do whatever you want — explore, gather, build, shape the terrain, climb the hill, dig, craft, or simply wander. There is no success or failure; the session ends at turn 200.
notes: Gen 3 Phase 1 substrate test. Larger world (64x64x4 = 4x area, 1 extra z-layer) and longer budget than Gen 1/2 sandboxes (32x32x3, 60t).
New affordances vs Gen 2: ladder block (placeable + climbable via 'interact up/down'), iron-ore deposits, secondary stone patch SW, scattered tree clusters at varied locations.

Observation target: what does a creature *do* when given more space, more time, and no goal? Builder vs explorer vs gatherer disposition was visible already in Gen 1 sandbox; the open world tests whether the disposition scales (more building? farther exploration?) or whether the lack of goal becomes paralyzing.
Terrain profile 'open_default' is deterministic given seed. Same seed = same world, so multiple creatures in this scenario can be compared on identical terrain.
